_about: Spec 35 (natural material colour) package 1: the appearance dimension of wood, separate from level, rarity and traits. A tree kind yields one wood species; the species gives a base sRGB colour, a colour family label, a grain tag and the per-log jitter a gathered log may vary within. Fields: species[id] = {name, color '#rrggbb', family, grain, variation{hue_deg[min,max], value[min,max]}, palette}; tree_kinds maps a nature_manifest family id (role tree/tree_dead) to one species; climate_overrides (optional) = {family: {climate: species}}. ASSUMPTION: the owner spec's eight wood palettes (mahogany, almond, oak, palm, maple, pine, walnut, ebony) are illustrative, not sampled game colours, so each species below borrows the spec row named in its 'palette' field and only species our tree kinds actually have are defined (birch, oak, acacia, palm, pine, snow pine, willow). ASSUMPTION: every tree kind maps to exactly one species; dead trees keep their living kind's species (they drop only branches, and a weathered dead-wood look is a later package). ASSUMPTION: the jitter is small (+/-5 deg hue, +/-0.07 value) so two logs of one species read as the same wood; the numbers are ours, the spec only asks for 'subtle natural variation'. ASSUMPTION: a lone stump (nature role prop, family tree_stump) drops wood_log too but carries no kind of its own, so it is mapped to oak, the default wood; a later package can key it on the island's climate. ASSUMPTION: 'oak' is the default species for a wood item gathered from an unmapped tree kind; existing saves get no look at all (see docs/current/inventory-bags.md).

palm.name: Palm
palm.palette: spec 35 Palm row (light tan / pale yellow)

snow_pine.name: Snow Pine
snow_pine.palette: spec 35 Pine row, bleached for the snowfield kind

_climate_overrides_about: ASSUMPTION: empty today (a tree kind yields one species). The loader honours {family: {climate: species}} so a later package can split a kind by climate without a code change.
